page: Amazon Web Services im4gn.8xlarge is a storage-optimized server instance powered by the AWS Nitro hypervisor and custom AWS Graviton processors. It features 32 dedicated physical cores on the arm64 architecture, utilizing the ARMv8 Neoverse-N1 model running at 2.5 GHz. The system is equipped with 128.0 GB of system memory, providing a balanced 4.0 GB of RAM per core. For storage-intensive workloads, the instance includes a bundled 15000 GB local NVMe SSD. Network connectivity is supported by a 50 Gbps baseline bandwidth, and the instance is optimized for both network and Elastic Block Store performance.

Benchmark data indicates average multi-core and memory performance alongside specific single-threaded limitations. The instance achieved a stress-ng multi-core CPU score of 48576.94 and a Geekbench multi-core score of 11490.0, both falling within the average range. Memory bandwidth is robust, with read-only small block cached speeds reaching 1893.97 GB/sec. However, single-core performance represents a notable tradeoff; the Geekbench single-core score of 941.0 and single-threaded gzip compression of 20.29 GB/sec are classified as weak, while single-threaded bzip3 decompression is poor at 7.01 GB/sec. LLM inference tasks also show mixed results, with average performance on 7B models but weak to poor throughput on smaller 135M models.

From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, the im4gn.8xlarge offers high local storage density and dedicated ARM-based compute resources, making it a viable option for workloads that require substantial local NVMe capacity without the premium of x86 licensing. The instance is well-suited for database operations, as demonstrated by its average Passmark database score of 20399.25 and a Redis SET throughput of 38.19 million operations per second. It is also appropriate for static web serving, multi-threaded data decompression, and general-purpose storage-heavy applications, though it is less optimal for single-threaded processing or intensive LLM inference.
